title: The strict-local fibre of a pseudo-open immersion
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume that $|f|$ is a homeomorphism onto its image and that the natural map of sheaves of rings $f^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ is an isomorphism. For any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar x=f\bar y$ and form strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] using the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$. The canonical map $Y_{(\bar y)}\to X_{(\bar x)}$ is an isomorphism, and the natural map $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y\times_X X_{(\bar x)}$ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the commutative square with top arrow $Y_{(\bar y)}\to Y$, bottom arrow $X_{(\bar x)}\to X$, and right arrow $f$ is Cartesian. All arrows are the canonical maps induced by $f$ and the pointed strict localizations.
